title: Everest Diagnostics pilot intake — raw call notes
content:
Call: Everest Diagnostics pilot kickoff (RM/infra/ML lead)
Date: 2024-11-19 09:30 PT
Attendees: Dr. Anil Rao (Everest tech lead), Priya Sharma (product), Jake Holloway (network), Maya Patel (Redwood SE), Ethan Brooks (Redwood SRE)
Call length: ~55m

Objective: capture on-prem/VPC constraints, desired model behavior, throughput targets for triage assistant, and initial success criteria for the pilot.

High-level ask from Everest:
- Replace rule-based triage emails with LLM-driven triage assistant that ingests recent patient notes (de-identified copy) and generates a prioritized action list + suggested coding (CPT/ICD hints).
- Pilot scope: 2 clinics, ~1200 messages/week, bursty arrival (morning peaks), document lengths vary 400–2,500 chars.
- Strong privacy/compliance requirement: cannot allow PHI to leave their VPC; Redwood Private (VPC) or on-prem package mandatory.

Key success metrics (customer-specified):
- Precision on suggested codes >= 85% on sampled test set
- Average response latency <= 1.2s for short notes (< 600 chars), <= 2.8s for long notes (1,500+ chars) at p95
- Throughput: baseline 4 qps sustained per clinic, occasional bursts to 12 qps for 2–3 minute windows
- 99.9% availability during business hours (8am–6pm client local)

Technical details discussed / requirements:
- Data flow constraints: all inference must run inside customer's VPC; metadata and telemetry can be forwarded to Redwood control plane over a customer-approved outbound egress IP range and mutual TLS. No raw PHI allowed in control plane. (Jake stressed strict egress audit.)
- KMS: customer uses HashiCorp Vault enterprise + HSM. They want Redwood to integrate with their KM via KMS connectors or run with customer-managed keys for model encryption and audit. Need an onboarding doc for HSM integration.
- Network: strict deny-by-default firewall. Required ports for node management: list to be provided by Redwood infra team. They will need a short-lived SSH jump host for initial hands-on install; require step-down approvals.
- Audit logs: 1 year retention in their Splunk cluster + event-forwarding from Redwood Private runtime. Need mapping of audit fields (request_id, model_version, input_hash (not raw content), duration_ms, node_id, user_token_id).
- Data residency: all cached KV prefixes must be stored on local encrypted volumes; no persistent backups are allowed to leave cluster.

Model & runtime preferences:
- Customer prefers an open model (no closed weights) that can be quantized if needed. Suggested starting model: 13B instruction-tuned family. They are open to trying a distilled 30B if accuracy suffers.
- Tokenization: many clinical terms and shorthand; we expect token distribution skew. We should run a tokenization pass on a small sample of notes (they will provide 200 anonymized notes by 2024-11-26).
- Sequence length: many notes < 1,000 tokens, but some discharge summaries hit 4,000 tokens. For pilot we will limit to 2,048 context window and evaluate longer-document handling with chunking + retrieval. Need to outline chunking strategy and evaluation plan.
- Caching & batching: customer wants predictable latency — prefer small batching windows + dynamic batching thresholds. Proposed starting config: max batch size 8, batching delay 20ms; measure p95 and iterate.

Operational expectations & SLOs:
- Canary deploys must be scheduled during off-peak with warmup. They want automatic traffic rollback on regression (quality or latency) and ability to pin to an older model if a new model underperforms.
- Nightly synthetic prompt runs to catch regressions on a golden prompt set (we should propose a 100-example golden set, they currently have 40 curated cases).
- Observability: per-request token counts, latency breakdown (queue, attention, kernel), model version in traces. They requested linkable traces to their Splunk traces.

Gotchas / constraints called out on the call:
- PHI leakage risk with offloading embeddings to third-party vector DBs. They want embeddings hosted inside VPC and prefer Redwood's managed vector store deployed in-vpc or the ability to bring their own (e.g., Milvus) with private networking.
- GPU sizing: Their infra team prefers reserved H100s but is concerned about cost. We discussed A100 80GB for 13B quantized runs; need to provide memory/throughput numbers for candidate models and quantization profiles (fp16, int8, awq) for 8k vs 2k contexts.
- DNS and cert provisioning may take time (internal CA). This might block mutual TLS until PKI is onboarded — estimate 2–3 weeks if there are hiccups.
- Regulatory: clinical sign-off required for any auto-suggested coding used in billing — pilot must clearly label suggestions as "assistant suggestions" and include confidence metadata.

Onboarding artifacts they asked for (explicit asks):
- Step-by-step Private deploy checklist (network, certs, KMS, minimum node sizing)
- Proposed model/quantization matrix for 7B/13B/30B candidates with expected p95 latency at 1–4 qps and memory footprints
- Sample audit schema and Splunk ingestion example
- A minimal terraform module or helm chart fragment for their infra team to review

Action items / next steps (owners + due dates):
- Everest: provide 200 anonymized sample notes and current golden cases (due 2024-11-26) — owner: Priya
- Redwood (Maya): tokenization pass + quick analysis (vocab gaps, avg tokens per note) once samples arrive (target 2 business days after samples)
- Redwood (Ethan): produce initial sizing/throughput estimate for 13B quantized on A100/ H100 (due 2024-11-29)
- Redwood (Infra): draft Private deploy checklist + required ports and egress IPs (due 2024-11-30) — owner: Lina
- Joint: schedule a controlled POC install window (3 days) for on-prem pilot (tentative: 2024-12-09 to 2024-12-11); Jake to confirm maintenance windows by 2024-11-27
- Redwood: assemble a 100-example synthetic golden set by seeding with their 40 curated cases + 60 generated but realistic clinical scenarios (internal ML/research to own, due 2024-12-06)

Notes to self / SE reminders:
- Request opt-in clause for telemetry at the API level: hashed input fingerprints only; include opt-out toggle for specific clinics.
- Prepare a short doc explaining chunking + retrieval vs extending context (pros/cons for clinical notes).
- Validate whether their Vault enterprise requires a specific PKCS#11 integration for HSM — if yes, collect their vendor/version.
- Confirm vector store encryption at rest + keywrap options for embedding caches.

Potential risks (escalation points):
- If PKI onboarding delays > 3 weeks, consider temporary air-gapped USB key exchange for initial bootstrap (expensive but possible) — escalate to legal for approvals.
- If quantized 13B doesn't meet precision target, escalate to model team for 30B evaluation and trade-offs on cost. Build a cost forecast for both options.

Rough timeline (high level):
- Week 0–2: samples + tokenization + sizing
- Week 3: infra prep + Private deploy checklist review
- Week 4: POC install and smoke tests
- Week 5–6: pilot metrics collection, iterate on batching and model config

Miscellaneous comments from Everest that may be useful later:
- Their triage team wants an "explain" toggle that returns short rationale bullets for each suggested code — useful for clinician acceptance.
- They currently use a homegrown de-identification pass; need to test whether de-id interferes with clinical abbreviations (e.g., 'SOB' vs 'shortness of breath').

Draft email snippet to send after call (to copy into follow-up):
"Thanks again for the kickoff. Attached are the checklist and the sample intake spreadsheet we discussed. Priya — if you can share the 200 anonymized notes by EOW (11/26) we’ll run a tokenization and sizing pass and get initial throughput numbers back by Friday. Lina and team — we’ll send the minimal port list and terraform fragment by 11/30. Looking forward to the POC install window in December. - Maya"

End of notes.
